headerLines: INTRODUCTION TO STATISTICAL AND PROBABILISTIC METHODS
parts.scriptNote: Use a separate Answer-Script for each part
parts.instructions: Answers must be brief and to-the-point. Give proper units wherever applicable.

rows.topic: Classical vs Frequency Definition of Probability
rows.textLatex: Distinguish between 'Classical Definition of Probability' and 'Probability As A Measure of Frequency of Occurrence of Random Event'.

rows.topic: Statistical Independence of Random Events
rows.textLatex: Introduce the concept of 'Statistical Independence of Random Events'. Explain its effect on ascertaining the joint probability of occurrence of random events.

rows.topic: Mean and Variance of Discrete Random Variable
rows.textLatex:
A voltage $X$ can take on any value (Volt) in the set $\{-3, -2, -1, 1, 2\}$ with same probability.
Find the mean and variance of
(i) $X$
(ii) $Y = -2X^2 + 3$

rows.topic: Cumulative Distribution Function & Discrete Expectations
rows.textLatex:
Errors in an experimental transmission channel are found when the transmission is checked by a certifier, that detects missing pulses. The number of bits in error, found in an eight-bit byte, is a random variable $X$ with the following distribution.
$$F(x) = \begin{cases} 0 & \text{for } x < 1 \\ 0.5 & \text{for } 1 \le x < 3 \\ 0.8 & \text{for } 3 \le x < 5 \\ 0.9 & \text{for } 5 \le x < 7 \\ 1 & \text{for } 7 \le x \end{cases}$$
What is $F(x)$ known as ? Sketch the probability density function of $X$. Determine $P(X = 5)$, $P(X \le 4)$, $P(X > 6)$, $P(2 \le X < 5)$ and the expectation of $X$.

rows.topic: Moment Generating Function & Exponential Distribution
rows.textLatex:
The probability density function for the diameter $D$ (in mm) of a drilled hole is
$$f(d) = 10e^{-10(d-5)} u(d-5).$$
Although the target diameter is $5\text{ mm}$, vibrations, tool wear, and other factors, produce diameters larger than $5\text{ mm}$. Obtain the expression for the 'Moment Generating Function'.
Hence obtain the expectation, the standard deviation, and the coefficient of skewness for the random variable $D$ (diameter).
Also find out the probability of $D \ge 5.1\text{ mm}$.

rows.topic: Expectation and Variance of Gamma Distribution
rows.textLatex: For a Gamma distributed random variable $Y$, obtain the expressions for the expectation and the variance, in terms of the shaping parameter and the scaling parameter.

rows.topic: Joint and Marginal Probability Density Functions
rows.textLatex:
It is claimed that the joint probability density function of two continuous random variables $U$ and $V$ is
$$\phi(u, v) = \frac{6}{5}(u + v^2)\text{ ; } 0 \le u \le 1, \; 0 \le v \le 1.$$
$$\phi(u, v) = 0 \text{ otherwise.}$$
Examine the validity of the claim. If it is valid, obtain the expressions for the marginal probability density functions. Also compute the probability
$$P\left(0 \le U \le \frac{1}{4},\; 0 \le V \le \frac{1}{4}\right).$$

rows.topic: Conditional Distribution and Bayes' Theorem for PDFs
rows.textLatex: Introduce the concept of conditional distribution of continuous random variable. Hence proceed to establish the Bayes' theorem involving probability density functions.

rows.topic: Statistical Independence and Uncorrelatedness
rows.textLatex: Show that, if two random variables are statistically independent, they are also statistically uncorrelated. Under such condition, find out the value of the correlation coefficient.

rows.topic: Independent Normal Random Variables
rows.textLatex: Let the random variables $X$ and $Y$ denote the lengths of two dimensions of a machined part, respectively. Assume that $X$ and $Y$ are statistically independent random variables, and further assume that the distribution of $X$ is normal with mean $10.5\text{ mm}$ and variance $0.0025\text{ mm}^2$ and that the distribution of $Y$ is normal with mean $3.2\text{ mm}$ and variance $0.0036\text{ mm}^2$. Determine the probability that $10.4\text{ mm} \le X \le 10.5\text{ mm}$ and $3.15\text{ mm} \le Y \le 3.25\text{ mm}$. Use the attached table of Standard Normal Distribution. Apply linear interpolation if necessary.

rows.topic: Correlation Coefficient for Linearly Related Variables
rows.textLatex: If two random variables are linearly related, what happens to their correlation coefficient? Explain with derivations.

rows.topic: WSS Random Process, Autocorrelation & Ergodicity
rows.textLatex:
The ensemble average of a wide-sense stationary random process $X[n]$ was measured at $n = 0$, and the value was obtained as $3$ units. The autocorrelation sequence of the random process is given by
$$R_X(n_1, n_2) = 9 + 4e^{-0.2|n_1 - n_2|}$$
Does the expression for the autocorrelation function reveal any other information regarding the stationarity and the ergodicity of the process? Determine the mean value, the variance and the correlation-coefficient values of the ensemble when $n_1 = 5$ and at $n_2 = 8$. Give necessary explanations.

rows.topic: White Noise & Spectral Description of Random Processes
rows.textLatex:
Write short note on any one of the following.
i) Ideal and bandlimited white noise.
ii) Spectral description of Random Processes.

rows.topic: Central Limit Theorem
rows.textLatex: What do you mean by Central Limit Theorem? How is it related with the mean and variance of the population? What are the assumptions made in the central limit theorem?

rows.topic: Bridge Load Normal & CLT Application
rows.textLatex: Civil engineers believe that $W$, the amount of weight (in units of $1,000$ pounds) that a certain span of a bridge can withstand without structural damage resulting, is normally distributed with mean $400$ and standard deviation $40$. Suppose that the weight (again, in units of $1,000$ pounds) of a car is a random variable with mean $3$ and standard deviation $.3$. How many cars would have to be on the bridge span for the probability of structural damage to exceed $.1$?

rows.topic: Chi-Square and t-Distribution of Sample Variance & Mean
rows.textLatex: If $\bar{X}$ is the sample mean and $S^2$ is the sample variance from a normal population with mean $\mu$ and standard deviation $\sigma$ then show that $(n-1)S^2/\sigma^2$ has a chi-square distribution with $(n-1)$ degrees of freedom and $\sqrt{n}(\bar{X} - \mu)/S$ has a $t$-distribution with $(n-1)$ degrees of freedom where $n$ is the sample size.

rows.topic: Maximum Likelihood Estimator for Normal Population
rows.textLatex: What do you mean by maximum Likelihood Estimator? What are the maximum likelihood estimator of the parameters relating to the normal distribution of the population?

rows.topic: Z-Test for Population Mean (Known Variance)
rows.textLatex:
A public health official claims that the mean home water used is normally distributed having mean, $\mu = 350$ gallons a day with $\sigma = 20$ gallons. To verify this claim, a study of $20$ randomly selected homes was performed with the results that the average daily water use of these $20$ homes were as follows:
340, 356, 332, 362, 318, 344, 386, 402, 322, 360, 362, 354, 340, 372, 338, 375, 364, 355, 324, and $370$.
Verify whether the data contradicts the officials claim with a test of $5\%$ significance level. Derive the expression that you have used for the test.

rows.topic: Critical Region for Normal Mean Test
rows.textLatex: What do you mean by the critical region? Derive the expression of critical region relating to the test concerning the mean of normal population when the variance is known.

rows.topic: Least Squares Estimators in Simple Linear Regression
rows.textLatex: Derive the expressions for the Least Square Estimators of the Regression Parameters of a simple linear regression model. Also, determine the expected values and variance of those parameters.

rows.topic: Sample Size Requirement & Type-II Error
rows.textLatex: Derive the expression of sample size requirement to meet certain specifications concerning type-II error.

rows.topic: Hypothesis Testing Definitions & Error Types
rows.textLatex: Define the terms, (i) Simple Hypothesis, (ii) Composite Hypothesis, (iii) Type I error, (iv) Type II error.
